submission.justification: Selection-S1 has the highest nominal significance (4.1 sigma at 50% efficiency in the 2025 summary), but its validation-region data/MC yield disagreement is 35%, far above the agreed 10% tolerance, because its jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled. That makes its background estimate non-robust, so it is excluded. Of the remaining candidates, Selection-S2 (6% disagreement, within tolerance) outperforms Selection-S3 (3% disagreement) on expected significance at every working point scanned: S2 peaks at 3.48 sigma at 60% signal efficiency (3.41 at 50%, 3.44 at 40%, 3.33 at 70%), versus a best of 2.68 sigma for S3 at 50%. The 60% working point lies within the 20–80% allowed range. Caveat: the significances are statistical-only, and S2's 6% yield disagreement should be carried as a systematic in the final result.

requirements.requirement: Selection must be one of the three strategies in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Selection-S2 (neural network on kinematic variables) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Background estimate must be robust (validation-region yield agreement within 10% tolerance)
requirements.evidence: Validation-region data/MC yield disagreement for S2 is 6%, within the 10% tolerance. S1 (35%) fails and was excluded; S3 (3%) also passes.
Recommended working point is 60% signal efficiency.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible expected signal significance (among robust options)
requirements.evidence: S2 at 60%: 3.478 sigma, the highest robust result scanned (S2 40%: 3.436, 50%: 3.409, 70%: 3.330; S3 best 2.675 at 50%). S1 nominally higher (4.1 sigma at 50% in the 2025 summary) but excluded on robustness grounds. Results are statistical-only.
